- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or 10% below recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model frequently underestimates downward moves; adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-neutral sentiment.
- Model overestimates short-term volatility in sentiment-driven periods; smooth 30d forecast by applying 3-period moving average to reduce noise.
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model often ignores trend reversal; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment >0.05 and price >10% below 14d high.
- Forecast horizon >14d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts; apply 1–2 day lag correction for sentiment-driven moves (e.g., if sentiment turns positive, delay forecast peak by 1–2 days).
